entries.title: Andy Weir is making an Full Cast Audible Audiobook
entries.summary: Audible built Exoplanet as a premium, full-cast audio experience complete with immersive Dolby Atmos sound design by Skywalker Sound. The post Andy Weir is making an Full Cast Audible Audiobook first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
Exoplanet is a highly anticipated sci-fi thriller launching on November 5, 2026, as an exclusive audio series on Audible. While heavily marketed with his name, the project is executive produced by Andy Weir—author of The Martian and Project Hail Mary—but is actually written by acclaimed novelist and comic book writer Benjamin Percy.

When the starship Wild Blue Yonder is torn apart by a quantum anomaly, each surviving crew member crash-lands in a different era on the same deadly exoplanet—hunted, alone, and running out of time. Chief Engineer Jeff Shaw (Anthony Mackie), aided by his virtual assistant (Ray Porter), must battle an unforgiving present, driven by one thing: getting home to his daughter. First Officer Becca Bang (Ariana DeBose) fights to survive a hostile alien past. Science Officer Logan Bowers (John Leguizamo) wakes in a machine-ruled future that shouldn’t exist. But the anomaly wasn’t random. A relentless alien intelligence is feeding on human technology—and it’s been waiting for them across every timeline. Separated by centuries, the crew must find a way to communicate across time itself before this world consumes them all. Blending heart-stopping action with the mind-bending science that Andy Weir is known for, Exoplanet explores what it means to fight for humanity’s future when your own existence hangs in the balance.

Andy Weir said, “I’m obsessed with problems, the kind where one person and a lot of math are all that stand between survival and disaster. Benjamin Percy’s writing in Exoplanet takes that and adds a twist that genuinely kept me up at night: what if the people trying to save each other were separated not by distance, but by centuries? You can’t see that story. You have to hear it. The crackle across a five-hundred-year gap, the desperation in a voice that doesn’t know if anyone’s still listening. Anthony, Ariana, and John don’t just perform it; they make you feel every impossible mile between them.”

Michael Kozlowski is the editor-in-chief at Good e-Reader and has written about audiobooks and e-readers for the past fifteen years. entries.title: The new Kobo Limited Edition cases are underwhelming
entries.summary: The Official Kobo Busy Bookworm Collector Case and Hopelessly Devoted are a highly popular, online-exclusive limited edition release specifically manufactured for Kobo's colour e-reader lineup. The post The new Kobo Limited Edition cases are underwhelming first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
Kobo has just released some new limited edition cases for the Kobo Libra Colour, Kobo Clara Colour, and the Kobo Clara BW. They cost around $44.99 CAD and come in two designs: Busy Bookworm or Hopelessly Devoted. Each of these Collector Cases features a semi-clear shell. However, these cases aren’t meant to protect your e-reader, since they only cover the back and not the e-paper display, which tends to get scratched easily by keys and other objects in a purse or messenger bag.

Official Kobo Limited Edition Collector Cases are online-exclusive, highly collectible releases designed specifically for the brand’s latest colour eReaders. These cases feature semi-clear snap-on back shells meant to show off your device’s accent colours while providing a canvas for custom bookish sticker decoration. Because they are produced in extremely small quantities, they do not restock once sold out.

Unlike standard folio cases, official Kobo Collector Cases only cover the back of your e-reader. They do not feature a front flip flap, a magnetic clasp, or auto sleep/wake functionality. If you purchase one of these cases, it is highly recommended to pair it with a protective travel sleeve to keep your display screen safe.

Kobo does not sell protective travel sleeves for its e-readers, so you would have to purchase one from Amazon, Etsy, or another 3rd-party marketplace.

entries.title: Onyx Boox will release the Palma 3 and other devices soon
entries.summary: Onyx BOOX wil soon release the Palma 3, Note Air6 C, Note Mini C, and BOOX Tab Elite. All of these devices will be geared towards the international market. The post Onyx Boox will release the Palma 3 and other devices soon first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
Onyx Boox is rumoured to be working on four new devices to release sometime this year. The Boox Palma 3, BOOX Note Air6 C, BOOX Note Mini C, and a new SKU called the BOOX Tab Elite. All of these devices will be geared towards the international market and include features such as Google Android OS and Google Play.

The BOOX Palma 3 has not been officially released yet, as the current top-tier models in Onyx Boox’s phone-sized e-paper lineup are the BOOX Palma 2 and the premium BOOX Palma 2 Pro. When Onyx Boox eventually introduces the Palma 3 generation, tech analysts expect it to address the remaining gaps in e-reader pocketability. It is heavily expected to transition to the Carta 1300 screen for sharper contrast and darker blacks. Moving past aging mid-range chipsets to a more modern, power-efficient octa-core processor to better sustain Boox Super Refresh technology.

The BOOX Note Air 6 C has not been officially released yet. Still, industry indicators suggest it is currently on the horizon as a highly anticipated successor to the Note Air 5 C. The device is heavily anticipated to ship with a newer Android version (likely Android 16), allowing for greater app longevity and smoother multitasking from the Google Play Store. It will almost certainly feature a faster, more power-efficient system-on-chip.

The BOOX Tab Elite is an upcoming, unreleased E-Ink device from Onyx. BOOX has not yet officially announced its specifications, pricing, or release date. Industry rumors and trademark filings suggest it will be a high-performance productivity tablet, likely succeeding or expanding upon the powerful Tab/Ultra series.

The Note Mini is a big unknown, but it could be an overdue replacement for the Tab Mini C, Boox’s smaller-screened 7.8″ colour e-ink tablet.

entries.title: Xteink X4 is being discontinued
entries.summary: The XTEINK X4 mini e-reader is now officially discontinued, and there will be no further production runs; the company is focusing on the X4 Pro. The post Xteink X4 is being discontinued first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
XTEINK has officially discontinued the original X4 pocket e-reader. On August 12, 2026, the company posted bittersweet goodbye messages across its social media channels—including Reddit, Instagram, and Facebook—confirming that the device is sold out and that there are no plans for future production.

Instead, the company is focusing on the upgraded XTEINK X4 Pro, which adds a touchscreen and a dual-tone (warm/cool) front light. Industry analysts note that by adding a touchscreen and a light, XTEINK can charge roughly 42% more for the Pro version over the basic entry-level hardware of the original X4, which boosts their profits.

The X4 might be discontinued, but they are working on the Xteink X4 Gen 2, an anticipated ultra-portable pocket e-reader from Xteink, designed as a thinner, lighter update with a larger battery compared to the original 4.3-inch minimalist device.

Update: Thank you so much for your support! XTEINK X4 is now officially sold out, and there are no plans for future production. We invite you to explore our X3 or X4 Pro models for your reading needs. Stay tuned for the upcoming new X4 series.

entries.title: Amazon Kindle Daily Deals Page has moved
entries.summary: Amazon has discontinued the Kindle Daily Deals page and now links to a more general one, with fewer deals. They are pushing their Book Deals Newsletter to compete against BookBub. The post Amazon Kindle Daily Deals Page has moved first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
Amazon has just changed the Kindle Daily Deals website for customers based in the United States. The new page is less of a deals page and looks like recommended book listings for Amazon, with no distinctive flavour. The old landing page now recommends that you subscribe to the Daily Deals Newsletter to get access to occasional better pricing.

The new Daily Deals landing page is nothing special; it lists a few carousels of deals, but primarily focuses on new books, pre-orders, and bestsellers, which are at full price. There are only two small sections devoted to sales that occur today and deals dropping in the future. The best savings on Kindle Books are via the newsletter.

The Kindle Daily Deals newsletter is an official Amazon email featuring a small, hand-picked set of daily Amazon discounts. In contrast, BookBub is a free, independent third-party service that lets you customize genre preferences and aggregates ebook sales across multiple retailers, including Amazon, Kobo, and Apple.

entries.title: Kindle Jailbreak Véra works on newer e-readers
entries.summary: Véra is an on-device software jailbreak for modern Amazon Kindle e-readers. It lets users install KOReader without needing a computer. The post Kindle Jailbreak Véra works on newer e-readers first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
There is a new jailbreak method that is available for Kindle e-readers called Véra. It works on most Kindles and Kindle Scribes running firmware 5.17.1 – 5.19.2. It uses your Kindle’s internet browser to set up and install, without the need to download and install scripts from your computer.

Véra works on the Kindle Colorsoft, Kindle Scribe, and all of the 11th- and 12th-generation Kindle e-readers. Most of the other jailbreaks that are available only work with outdated firmware on very old devices.

One of the big advantages of using a modern jailbreak is being able to install KOReader, which is a document viewer for E Ink devices. Supported file formats include EPUB, PDF, DjVu, XPS, CBT, CBZ, FB2, PDB, TXT, HTML, RTF, CHM, DOC, MOBI and ZIP files. It’s available for Kindle, Kobo, PocketBook, Android and desktop Linux.

KindleModding has post-jailbreak instructions! If you don’t end up liking KOReader, you can just choose not to use it — a jailbreak doesn’t change or remove any stock Kindle functionality, so there’s not really a reason to revert the jailbreak. But yes, it is possible to un-jailbreak if you want or need to (the most common use case would be sending it in for warranty repair or reselling it). You can unjailbreak by restoring OTA updates, factory resetting, then installing a firmware binary.

entries.title: Barnes and Noble NOOK e-readers and apps have missing cover art
entries.summary: The Barnes and Noble NOOK line of e-readers, tablets, and apps is not displaying e-book cover art properly, with no estimated timeline for a possible fix. The post Barnes and Noble NOOK e-readers and apps have missing cover art first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
Barnes and Noble NOOK e-readers have been plagued by an issue for NOOK Books, that have missing cover images in a users library. These missing book covers effect books purchased directly from the online bookstore that is accessible on the devices such as the NOOK Glowlight 4, NOOK Glowlight 4 Plus and their tablets that are running the NOOK Hub. The apps for Android and iOS are also suffering from this issue, as is the library on the B&N website that lists all of the purchased books.

The missing e-book cover art has been an ongoing issue for the past three weeks and it still has not been solved yet with a software update, it seems the technical support team has been unaware of this issue, primarily because they sell way more hardcover and paperbacks than they do e-books or audiobooks. It looks like the metadata is not working properly, so hardly any images show up, but once inside of the book, the text is working properly.

Good e-reader has reached out to B&N since this issue occurred and they said “We understand and apologize for the ongoing issue related to your NOOK covers being blank. We have identified this issue and our backend team is working on it. A fix will be implemented in the near future so we kindly ask that you allow some time for the fix to be added in. Please check for software updates for the /web browser to ensure it has been updated added once it is available. Thank you for your patience and understanding in this matter.”

entries.title: Beyond eBooks: Optimizing Modern E-Ink Tablets for Casual Web Gaming and Digital Leisure
entries.summary: The Social Connection: Comparing Book Club Communities and Interactive Online Lobbies. The post Beyond eBooks: Optimizing Modern E-Ink Tablets for Casual Web Gaming and Digital Leisure first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
Remember the early days of e-readers? If you owned one of those first-generation devices, you will probably recall how they did one thing brilliantly and absolutely nothing else. They were digital books, plain and simple. If you tried to load a webpage on their rudimentary browsers, you were met with a painful flashing screen and a system that felt like it was running through thick treacle. It was a novel technology, quite literally, but it was strictly limited to black-and-white text.

Times have changed dramatically. Over the last few years, e-paper technology has quietly undergone a massive shift. We have moved far beyond the simple monochrome novels of the past. Today, we have versatile e-ink tablets running full versions of Android, complete with colour displays and processors that can handle much more than static text. Brands like Onyx Boox, Bigme, and even Kobo have completely changed our expectations of what these paper-like screens can achieve. With access to app stores and full internet browsers, these devices are no longer just for reading; they are multi-functional tools for work, creative sketching, and casual, low-intensity entertainment.

This evolution opens up a world of possibilities for how we spend our down time, allowing us to rethink our relationship with screens. If you have ever wanted to browse the web, check in with an online community, or enjoy light interactive apps without the eye strain of a standard tablet, modern e-paper devices have finally become capable enough to make that a reality.

Technical Performance: Benchmarking Web Browsers and Interactive Scripts on E-Paper Screen Tech

To understand how far these devices have come, it is worth looking at how they actually handle interactive web content. Traditional tablets use LCD or OLED screens that refresh sixty to one hundred and twenty times every second. E-ink screens, however, work by physically moving tiny microcapsules of black, white, and sometimes coloured pigment using electrical charges.

In the past, every single change on the screen required a full refresh, which meant a noticeable black-and-white flash. If you tried to scroll down a webpage, the constant flashing was enough to make anyone give up. Modern Android-powered e-ink tablets have solved this by offering sophisticated, customizable refresh modes.

Most modern devices offer several distinct screen modes:

  • Regal Mode: High detail, minimal ghosting, but a slower refresh rate. Perfect for reading static text.
  • A2/Speed Mode: A faster refresh rate with slightly lower image quality. Great for scrolling through articles.
  • Ultrafast/X-Mode: The fastest available setting, designed to handle animation and interactive elements smoothly.

When you load a modern web browser like Chrome or Kiwi on an e-paper tablet, the device has to interpret complex JavaScript and CSS layouts. Surprisingly, mid-range and premium e-ink tablets now breeze through these tasks thanks to improved processors and dedicated graphics processing units. While you certainly won’t be running intensive 3D applications, standard web scripts, animated menus, and interactive buttons respond with impressive speed.

The main challenge is “ghosting,” which is when faint remnants of previous images remain on the screen. Modern software handles this by triggering subtle, partial refreshes behind the scenes, ensuring that scrolling through an online article or clicking an interactive link feels responsive and usable. It is a fascinating balance between hardware and software, ensuring that your digital leisure time is as seamless as possible.

Screen-Time Harmony: Transitioning to Eye-Safe Nighttime Entertainment and Casual Games

Many of us are trying to find a better balance with our screen time, especially during the evening. We know the routine; you have finished a busy day, you want to wind down, but staring at a bright, blue-light-emitting smartphone screen right before sleep isn’t doing your eyes or your sleep cycle any favours. This is where the beauty of e-paper really shines. Because these screens reflect ambient light rather than shining light directly into your eyes, they are incredibly gentle on the eyesight.

If you want to transition to a more relaxed evening routine without giving up digital entertainment entirely, an Android-powered e-ink tablet is an ideal companion. Instead of mindlessly scrolling through stressful news feeds or social media, you can opt for casual, low-intensity web-based activities. For instance, playing a few rounds of web-optimized bingo on your e-paper device offers a lovely way to wind down.

Because e-ink screens do not emit the harsh blue light of traditional displays, you can enjoy this kind of casual entertainment in bed without disrupting your body’s natural melatonin production. It is a slower, more deliberate form of leisure that doesn’t bombard your senses. By choosing a paper-like display, you can keep your mind active and engaged in a friendly, low-stress environment while ensuring that your body is physically preparing for a deep, natural sleep.

The Social Connection: Comparing Book Club Communities and Interactive Online Lobbies

Reading is often thought of as a solitary pursuit, but the rise of digital reading clubs and community platforms has turned it into a highly social activity. Many e-ink users love to share their thoughts, discuss plot developments, and connect with people who share their interests. Modern e-ink tablets handle these community hubs beautifully, allowing readers to jump into forums, write reviews, and participate in discussion boards directly from their devices.

This social aspect isn’t limited to book clubs. If you look at casual web platforms, the sense of community is just as strong. For example, when you participate on a friendly, interactive bingo platform, a massive part of the experience is the live chat and the friendly interaction with other players. Modern colour e-paper devices are now perfectly capable of handling these lightweight, collaborative web portals.

You can easily keep an eye on a chat lobby, type messages to other participants, and feel part of a wider community, all on a screen that feels as comfortable to read as a paperback. It bridges the gap between solitary reading and real-time socialising, showing just how versatile these devices have become. Whether you are discussing a classic novel or celebrating a win with other players, the social experience remains engaging, clear, and easy on the eyes.

Optimisation Guide: Adjusting Refresh Rates and Settings for Web-Based Apps on E-Paper

To get the absolute best out of your e-ink tablet when using web apps or playing casual games, a little bit of tweaking goes a long way. Because these devices are primarily designed for reading, their default settings are rarely optimized for interactive web elements. Here are a few quick adjustments you can make to improve your experience:

  • Select the Right Refresh Mode: Switch your tablet’s refresh rate to a faster setting, such as “Speed” or “X-mode,” when loading interactive websites. This reduces ghosting and makes animations much smoother.
  • Boost the Contrast: Web pages often use light grey text on white backgrounds, which can be hard to see on e-paper. Go into your tablet’s app optimization settings and increase the dark colour enhancement to make text and buttons pop.
  • Adjust the DPI (Dots Per Inch): If buttons or chat boxes look too small, increase the DPI in your browser settings. This makes interactive elements larger and much easier to tap accurately on an e-ink screen.
  • Warm Up the Front Light: If you are playing or reading in the evening, adjust the built-in front light to a warm, amber tone. This minimizes eye strain and creates a cosy, relaxing atmosphere for your nighttime leisure.

By taking a couple of minutes to customize these settings, you can turn your e-ink tablet into a highly capable, comfortable device for all your casual web-based activities.

Please remember to keep your leisure activities safe and enjoyable. If you choose to participate in casual online play, always play responsibly and set sensible limits.

Markus lives in San Francisco, California and is the video game and audio expert on Good e-Reader! He has a huge interest in new e-readers and tablets, and gaming.

entries.title: Instapaper now comes pre-installed on BOOX devices
entries.summary: Sign in to Instapaper on your Palma device by opening the pre-installed Instapaper app from your home screen. The post Instapaper now comes pre-installed on BOOX devices first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
Instapaper now comes pre-installed on BOOX Palma 2 and Palma 2 Pro devices. The Instapaper app on Palma 2 and Palma 2 Pro supports all core Instapaper features, including syncing your articles with your Instapaper account and saving articles to your Instapaper account. Like, archive, delete articles, and access articles offline, and Highlights and notes.

BOOX is a global leader in E Ink electronics, specializing in E Ink tablets and monitors. Its product lineup spans 6-inch to 13.3-inch devices, helping ambitious, persistent, and innovative users boost productivity in work and study — without straining their eyes. The BOOX Palma series brings this experience to a pocket-sized, one-handed E Ink reader featuring a color E Ink display, an adjustable warm-to-cool front light, a fingerprint sensor, and an Android system with Google Play support.

entries.title: Barack Obama is hosting a new podcast on Audible
entries.summary: Barack Obama is set to host a podcast on Audible about books that have profoundly shaped his worldview and our society. The post Barack Obama is hosting a new podcast on Audible first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
Barack Obama is hosting a new podcast titled A Great Book with Barack Obama, scheduled to premiere exclusively on Audible on September 24, 2026. The six-episode series is a collaboration between Audible and Higher Ground, the media production company founded by Barack and Michelle Obama.

Obama will sit down with six distinct “luminaries”—including writers, thinkers, and artists—to dissect the literary works that heavily impacted his life, perspective, and worldview. The conversations aim to address identity, power, memory, culture, and why storytelling matters in modern society. While the production companies have confirmed the guest list features compelling contemporary voices, the specific names of his interviewees are yet to be announced.

“The six books featured in this series have stayed with me throughout my life, and each one has something to teach us about the human experience,” he said.

“For this podcast, I invited some friends to explore why they resonate, how they can shape our understanding of ourselves and each other, and why literature matters now more than ever. I hope listeners will be inspired to discover or rediscover books that change the way they see themselves and the world.”

Barack Obama is no stranger to books; he releases reading lists twice a year. The latest was his Summer Reading List, featuring a curated selection of 11 compelling fiction and non-fiction titles. This annual tradition highlights contemporary authors and stories that address identity, politics, history, and human resilience.
